items.title: Cyberpunk 2 might include multiplayer quests after CD Projekt Red scrapped the feature in Cyberpunk 2077
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077's sequel may include online functionality, as a new CDPR job listing asks for an "understanding of multiplayer network architecture."
items.content:
Image credit: CDPR News by Kaan Serin Contributor Published on Oct. 28, 2026, 5:56 p.m. Follow Cyberpunk 2 Prioritise us on Google Cyberpunk 2 might try to revive Cyberpunk 2077 's online ambitions, as a new CD Projekt Red job listing is looking for someone familiar with "multiplayer network architecture."

As spotted by Cheap Happens , the role-playing powerhouse is currently looking to hire a lead quest programmer for its upcoming open-world sequel. Buried away at the bottom of the job listing , under the "Nice To Haves" section, the studio asks for an "understanding of multiplayer network architecture and client-server synchronization for game state/ quests."

The multiplayer mention is by no means confirmation that Cyberpunk 2 - or whatever it ends up being called - will have co-op and other online modes, but it's definitely something CD Projekt Red is looking into. And it certainly makes sense, too.

Once upon a time, Cyberpunk 2077 was intended to receive a multiplayer portion sometime after its initial launch. Of course, at the time, the shaky state of the game's development meant that was no longer feasible and CD Projekt Red instead said multiplayer would come as its own "triple-A release." Eventually, the famed studio realised it simply had to focus on ensuring the base game was stable enough on its own, and shelved those online ambitions.

A few years back, Cyberpunk 2077's senior quest designer, Philipp Weber, told Eurogamer the company was "focusing on bringing online into all of our franchises one day" by "building an online technology that can be seamlessly integrated into development of our future games."

More recently, in 2024, CD Projekt CEO Adam Badowski said the team were "considering" multiplayer elements for the Cyberpunk sequel back when the game was still in its early concept phases.

We don't know much else about the neon-drenched follow-up, but CDPR has been keeping series fans full and fed with continual updates to Cyberpunk 2077. Earlier this week, the game got an update celebrating the debut of Cyberpunk Edgerunners Season 2 on Netflix - everything from dual-wielding to cross-platform mods were added to the six-year-old game.

items.title: CDPR Job Listing Hints at Cyberpunk 2 Co-op
items.summary: With excitement swirling after Edgerunners Season 2, CD Projekt RED has put new job listings for a future Cyberpunk title featuring co-op gameplay.
items.content:
Add DualShockers on Google Add as Preferred Source By Michael Manning Published Oct 27, 2026, 2:37 PM EDT Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of art has something worth celebrating. He's excited to bring this outlook to Dualshockers. Sign in to your DualShockers account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Despite having only a single title, Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the biggest RPGs in the world, standing alongside modern classic titles like Skyrim and Fallout to define how gamers see big-budget RPGs. Riding another burst of hype with Edgerunners Season 2, CD Projekt RED is already looking to the future, with some very interesting whispers circling as we speak.

Multiple former and current EA employees spoke anonymously about the current state of the company, and it wasn't a pretty picture.

In a job posting made just hours ago, CD Projekt RED has sent out feelers for a Lead Quest Programmer meant to put together major quest lines alongside writers and designers.

Among the bonus requirements for this role is a request for an "Understanding of multiplayer network architecture and client-server synchronization for game state/quests." Most players surmise this could only really mean one thing.

Co-op has been a long-desired wish for the original Cyberpunk 2077, with plenty of attempts at modding in the option to mixed results. From a baseline, 2077 is built to be a single-player experience, meaning adding effective co-op requires retooling most of the game. Looking at just how choppy most of V's third person animations are, it's very clear CD Projekt RED wasn't too worried about how you'd be perceived from the outside.

After plenty of patches, most centered on recovering from the game's infamously scuffed launch, 2077 is in a fantastic spot, sitting alongside titles like No Man's Sky and Wuthering Waves when it comes to big improvements. With the open secret that CD Projekt RED are working on the sequel, fan speculation has been over the moon, and this job listing makes hints at multiplayer being at least a consideration.

From a baseline, 2077 is built to be a single-player experience, meaning adding effective co-op requires retooling most of the game.

That already makes the theoretical Cyberpunk 2 more co-op ready than its predecessor, and the desire for a baseline 'understanding of multiplayer' means it could take many different forms. Not specifying co-op is very exciting. Imagine some light PvP elements, like the Watch Dogs series' invasions, where a player-controlled Netrunner could sneak into your game to cause havic, assisting NPC faction members to fight off the host player.

Both seasons of Edgerunners, the Cyberpunk sister series written directly by CD Projekt RED, give different framings of how a group of individuals can thrive and clash in Night City, really opening up the potential of how the sequel might frame multiplayer. Whether its players from different worlds slowly getting pulled into each other's stories or full squads running jobs, the possibilities feel endless.

The real discussion to be had here, however, is whether or not CD Projekt RED can manage a solid RPG story while implementing co-op shenanigans. Starting with The Witcher franchise, where the company focuses most of its efforts, CDPR is known for incredibly solid single-player experiences devoid of multiplayer trappings.

Their only multiplayer venture is Gwent, a digital card game based on a mini-game in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, which has maintained a niche following since its launch. Developing a story-based title for multiple players is very different from a single-player one, and CD Projekt Red is clearly taking their time before they officially announce any implementation.

CD Projekt RED's newest upcoming title, The Witcher 4 , is another standard single-player venture, and the job listing for Cyberpunk 2 noting the multiplayer experience as optional, reads to me like they're interested in exploring the possibility, but far from married to it. When following up as big a title as Cyberpunk 2077, your options are to play it safe or totally redefine the experience, and with it so far out, we have no way of knowing which route CD Projekt RED will take.

Their continuous love for the original 2077, including a new update to coincide with Edgerunners' second season, is telling. Cyberpunk was a massive departure for the studio, one that crumbled, but landed on its feet incredibly well. With another chance in the driver's seat, I can't wait to see what else comes in Night City's future.

One of the gods of story-driven role-playing games.

items.content:
By Willa Rowe Published Oct 27, 2026, 2:23 PM EDT Willa Rowe is a contributing writer at Polygon, covering games and entertainment. She is a New York-based journalist and critic whose work has been featured in Kotaku, Digital Trends, the A.V. Club, GamesRadar+, and more. She also co-hosts the Girl Mode podcast. Image: CD Prokekt Red Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Cyberpunk 2077 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap A good sequel builds on what came before while retaining what worked the first time around. So with Cyberpunk 2 , the upcoming sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 , CD Projekt Red will likely want to retain the open-world William Gibson-esque fun of its 2020 RPG while giving players something new.

A new job listing from the developer reveals one way in which the sequel could liven things up, and fans are sure to be excited.

CD Projekt Red is currently looking to hire more developers for work on Cyberpunk 2 . One job listing (as spotted by Cheat Happens ) suggests the sequel will have a multiplayer component. In the listing's "Nice to Have" section, one bullet point reads, "Understanding of multiplayer network architecture and client-server synchronization for game state/quests."

While that mostly reads like a lot of tech speak, the multiplayer portion of that description speaks for itself. Cyberpunk 2077 was originally intended to receive multiplayer support after release, but that plan was scrapped. Bringing multiplayer back in some form for the sequel feels like an opportunity for CD Projekt Red to realize the grand vision it wasn't fully able to execute with Cyberpunk 2077 .

Incidentally, fans recently started the work of bringing co-op multiplayer to Cyberpunk 2077 with a new mod name NightCoop .

Image: CD Projekt Red The studio is pretty busy right now with a number of projects in different stages of development. Next year, The Witcher 3 will receive the new Songs of the Past expansion, which CD Projekt Red co-developed with Fool's Theory. After that, The Witcher 4 is currently slated for release in 2028, starting a new trilogy. Beyond that, a Witcher 1 remake is also in development, again alongside Fool's Theory.

Cyberpunk 2 will come sometime after The Witcher 4 , so don't expect it anytime soon. Even with all of this, CD Projekt Red has also revealed Project Hadar , which will be the studio's next standalone IP. Just this month, the studio revealed that the project is in "the earliest stages of the creative process, which means we are not developing any game yet, but working exclusively on the foundation for this new setting."

items.title: New Cyberpunk 2 Job Listing Further Supports Multiplayer Mode
items.summary: Multiplayer functionality could very well be on the cards for Cyberpunk 2, with previous job openings being backed up by a new one.
items.content:
Last year, new CDPR job listings showed the developer was toying with implementing multiplayer into a possible Cyberpunk sequel, and new Cyberpunk 2 job listings have only reiterated this.

Does Cyberpunk need multiplayer? Some will say yes; others will disagree. There’s no denying that a single-player Cyberpunk 2077 experience, once it worked, is a sensational journey that almost doubles as a pseudo co-op game, with Johnny Silverhand lingering as a consistent presence. But it looks like multiplayer is an eventuality more than a possibility for Cyberpunk 2.

In September 2025, we reported on new CDPR job listings, suggesting Cyberpunk 2 could feature online multiplayer , a big development considering how well the first game performed.

Fast forward over a year, and a new job listing for Cyberpunk 2 has been found. This role is a ‘Lead Quest Programmer’ working on ‘Cyberpunk 2’ for CD Projekt RED .

‘CD PROJEKT RED is looking for a Lead Quest Programmer to join the team working on Cyberpunk 2, the follow-up to Cyberpunk 2077 and the next major video game in the Cyberpunk franchise, led by our North American team centered in Boston.’

There are many roles within the job, and a lot of experience is required; however, it’s hard to look past the ‘Nice to Have’ section, mentioning skills that aren’t needed to apply but would be handy, essentially:

I’ve highlighted the key part. You don’t even need to speculate at this point; it seems quite clear CDPR is leaning into some sort of multiplayer addition to Cyberpunk 2077. We just don’t know if it’s online multiplayer, local co-op, online co-op, or something else entirely.

Would multiplayer help or hurt Cyberpunk 2? Let us know your thoughts on the Insider Gaming Discord server .

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Sequel Gets Official Release Update And Teaser
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077's highly anticipated sequel just got an interesting new update & teaser.
items.content:
Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Nicholas Becher Published Oct 27, 2026, 8:31 AM EDT Nicholas Becher is a gaming journalist with an MFA in Creative Writing from FAU. With extensive experience playing video games, he covers all forms of gaming content at Screen Rant, from breaking news to the latest fan theories. Most-played games range from Clair Obscur to Civ to Elden Ring to Halo 2 and beyond. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Cyberpunk 2077 's highly anticipated sequel, now known officially as Cyberpunk 2 and formerly operating under the codename Project Orion at CD Projekt Red, has received another intriguing development update as work continues on the ambitious follow-up.

Although an official release window remains unconfirmed, the sequel is expected to follow CDPR's upcoming Witcher 4 , which is currently targeting a 2028 launch. However, development on both franchises is already happening simultaneously, with CDPR steadily expanding its Cyberpunk 2 team as the project progresses.

While Cyberpunk fans were recently treated to a surprise update introducing a trove of free Edgerunners 2 content and major gameplay improvements to the original game, players are understandably eager to learn more about the highly anticipated sequel. However, during the Edgerunners 2 announcement event, we got a major update on Cyberpunk 2 's development that you may have missed during all the excitement, as well as a look at what's expected in the next game.

According to one of the lead developers on Cyberpunk 2 , associate game director Paweł Sasko (via TweakTown ), a surprisingly large portion of the sequel's quest development team consists of former modders who previously worked on CD Projekt Red's games. During a recent REDstreams presentation discussing Cyberpunk 2077 's Update 2.5, Sasko revealed that approximately half of the developers responsible for creating quests for the upcoming sequel originally got their start making fan-created mods.

Interestingly, many of these developers were already creating mods long before Cyberpunk 2077 was released, having previously worked on The Witcher 2 and The Witcher 3 as well. Discussing how modding can provide an entry point into professional game development, Sasko explained: "They were all modders before [Cyberpunk 2077] of The Witcher 3, Witcher 2, you know, before, and you know we hired them, and they're part of our company, and it's a wonderful way to actually start your career and really learn and see how to actually build those things."

It's an encouraging revelation for fans who have spent years enjoying the countless community-created projects available for CDPR's games, and will be a ray of hope that the next game will launch in a much better state than the original, which famously suffered tremendously from bugs and performance issues. Modders have consistently demonstrated their ability to expand existing experiences with relatively minimal performance problems, introducing everything from gameplay overhauls and visual improvements to entirely new missions and story-driven content.

Close Cyberpunk 2077 Male V on a yellow background. window.arrayOfGalleries["article-gallery-1-1323318879"] = '" Close Cyberpunk 2077  Male V on a yellow background. "'; More importantly, developing these mods often requires considerable technical expertise, creativity, and an understanding of the systems that make complex RPGs function. The fact that CDPR is actively recruiting from this community suggests the studio recognizes the value of those skills, particularly when developing the next generation of its flagship franchises.

For a little more context, Sasko's comments also coincided with Cyberpunk 2077 's latest update, which introduced cross-platform mod support, allowing players to browse and install supported community creations directly through the game. The developer believes making mods more accessible could encourage additional players to experiment with creating their own content, potentially opening doors for the next generation of professional devs.

Although Sasko's estimate doesn't necessarily indicate how many former modders are working on Cyberpunk 2 overall, their substantial presence on the quest team is especially noteworthy given how important storytelling was to the original game's success, and gives us a little teaser at the quality of quests in the next game.

Of course, it's too early to know exactly what these developers have planned for the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel, particularly since CDPR has yet to reveal any significant details about its narrative. Nevertheless, having some of the franchise's most passionate community creators directly involved in shaping its future certainly gives fans another reason to be optimistic.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Hotfix 2.500.200 Released on October 27
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 hotfix 2.500.200 is out on October 27, and while this resolves issues, there are still a lot of bugs that remain unsquashed.
items.content:
Following the release of Cyberpunk 2077’s big Edgerunners 2.5 patch last week, CD Projekt RED has released a follow-up hotfix aimed at resolving key issues that will appear as Cyberpunk 2077 update 2.500.200.

Before anyone gets too excited, today’s download does NOT resolve a lot of the problems players have been experiencing after applying the 2.5 patch — particularly, PS5/PS5 Pro players.

Clocking in at just 1 GB, read on for what to expect from today’s patch, as well as the issues we’ve managed to round up from the community.

Per CD Projekt RED, today’s update dows the following: “It fixes an issue players in Argentina were having with accessing their saved game data. Due to the nature of such fixes, players in other regions will also see this update pop up and download for them, but it doesn’t affect anything other than that particular issue.”

While getting a patch is good, there is a mountain of issues that have yet to be resolved, with some key ones listed below.

Not only that, but even on CD Projekt RED’s forums, one user has listed 15 bugs in a span of a two-hour playthrough on the PS5 Pro.

Hopefully, CDPR releases a patch to resolve some of these issues soon. If we do get one, expect it here on MP1st.

In related news, Activision seems to be developing its own open-world game to combat Cyberpunk and Grand Theft Auto.

items.title: I played Cyberpunk 2077 for free in my browser with a budget laptop
items.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 in your browser for FREE? We put it to the test, and the results might surprise you. 🎮
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 is playable for free in your browser, and we've put it to the test.

Cyberpunk 2077 fans can now play CD Projekt RED's popular RPG in Google Chrome for free, without cloud gaming.

Not long ago, we never imagined huge games like CD Projekt RED's Cyberpunk 2077 could be played for free in a browser. But as we've seen with the 128-player browser version of Halo: Combat Evolved, things that once seemed impossible are now a reality.

Of course, this is an unofficial project created by omonkeyzz and isn't affiliated with CD Projekt RED . How long it will remain online is unclear, especially as similar browser projects have disappeared after gaining attention.

Unlike cloud gaming services such as GeForce NOW, this version runs on your own PC rather than streaming from a remote server. The game loads through your browser, so there's no need for a traditional installation, although you'll still need a capable PC to play it.

The browser version of Cyberpunk 2077 uses WebAssembly (Wasm) to run compiled code directly in your browser, while WebGPU allows it to use your PC's graphics hardware to render the game's 3D world. This means the game runs on your own hardware rather than being streamed from a remote server, although the browser still needs to load game data to get everything running.

The browser version also doesn't include the Phantom Liberty expansion, although that could potentially change in the future. Of course, there's no guarantee how long the project will remain available online. As it's still relatively new, you're also likely to encounter some bugs, and even a high-end PC might not run it as smoothly as the official version.

It's worth noting that, as impressive as this browser version of Cyberpunk 2077 is, it does have its limitations, which will largely depend on your PC's capabilities. Even though it runs in a browser, your hardware still has to handle the game's graphics and processing demands. I tried playing it on my budget laptop and, let's just say, it struggled. However, I can confirm that it works and includes features such as choosing your Lifepath and full character customisation.

After you've finished creating your character, you can begin playing and exploring Night City, much as you would in the official release.

Loading the game can also take a while, unlike the browser version of Halo: Combat Evolved , which loads almost instantly. Cyberpunk 2077 is a much more demanding game, and the browser needs time to load the relevant game data and compile shaders before you can get started.

READ MORE: 13 best Cyberpunk 2077 mods that feel essential for PC players

While the browser version of Cyberpunk 2077 is primarily designed for PC, it has reportedly worked on some modern Android phones. However, compatibility and performance can vary depending on your device, and support for iPhone, iPad and tablets isn't fully confirmed. That being said, it's not something we'd recommend trying right now.

Yes, I'd say so. Even if it struggles to run on your system, it's worth trying out of pure curiosity. It's impressive to see what's possible with modern web browsers.

However, we'd still recommend playing the official release of Cyberpunk 2077 , whether you're on PC, PlayStation, Xbox or Nintendo Switch 2. The official release offers the full game experience, and depending on the platform and edition, you can also access post-launch content and updates. The Phantom Liberty expansion is sold separately or included in certain editions and bundles.

items.title: Playden Turns Jailbroken PS5 Consoles Into Steam Machines, With Cyberpunk 2077, Resident Evil 4, and Many More Windows Games
items.summary: Through a launcher called Playden, users with a jailbroken PS5 can now log on Steam and play Windows games on PlayStation 5 consoles.
items.content:
A new homebrew project called Playden lets users run Windows games from their Steam libraries on jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles . The open-source launcher uses a PS5 port of Wine to run Windows software, creating a separate environment for each game and even placing individual titles directly on the console's Home screen.

The project arrives following fast-paced progress in the PS5 homebrew scene . As we previously reported , leaked Level 0 BootROM keys would eventually open the door to permanent custom firmware and broader emulation on existing consoles. Earlier this month, a separate PSBOX client has already brought Xbox Cloud Gaming to hacked systems . Playden is another sign that the scene is moving beyond proof-of-concept exploits and toward practical software.

To be clear, though, Playden is not a PS5 emulator or a way to run pirated games . According to its GitHub repository , it is a launcher for a jailbroken PS5 that signs in to the user's real Steam account, displays their library, downloads games covered by their licenses, and launches Windows versions via prospero-win, a Wine port for the PS5. Users can also import Windows game folders from USB storage, an M.2 SSD, or via FTP without signing in to Steam . Each game receives its own private Windows environment, or bottle, so settings and files do not overlap. Playden also creates a separate PS5 app and Home screen tile for each title, allowing users to launch games without opening the launcher.

The project supports Steam Cloud saves, per-game graphics and controller settings, and multiple graphics translation paths . Direct3D 8 through 11 games run through DXVK, Direct3D 12 through vkd3d-proton, OpenGL through Mesa's Zink, and some titles can use Vulkan directly. It also maps the DualSense as an Xbox controller for compatible Windows games.

The project's compatibility document, last updated two days ago , lists games tested on PS5 firmware 13.60, along with community reports on other firmware versions. There's already a fairly substantial number of working titles , ranging from indie games such as Celeste, Hollow Knight, Vampire Survivors, and Papers, Please to triple-A releases including Cyberpunk 2077 and Resident Evil 4 .

The Cyberpunk 2077 entry is particularly interesting. The tester reports that the game reaches menus, character creation, the Nomad opening, and garage gameplay, using roughly 3 GB of video memory during a 13-minute session. However, the entry also notes that the frame rate has not yet been measured , which illustrates why these reports should be read as compatibility tests rather than full-fledged performance benchmarks.

As you'd expect, not everything works at this stage. Armored Core VI: Fires of Rubicon, Counter-Strike 2, Hades II, Hi-Fi Rush, Marvel Rivals, and Shin Megami Tensei V: Vengeance are all currently listed as broken. Common blockers include anti-cheat systems, Denuvo, launchers that require starting additional programs, insufficient file handle limits, and Direct3D feature-level requirements .

Playden is explicitly labeled as alpha software, and its developer, leolobato , warns that it signs in to a real Steam account, stores the Steam session token on the console without encryption, and writes to Steam Cloud saves. A bug could therefore overwrite newer cloud saves with older or broken ones . It also requires a jailbroken console, root-level helpers, and payloads such as kstuff, ShadowMountPlus, and an ELF loader to run after each boot.

Furthermore, a running game can obtain elevated rights on the console, meaning users should only run games they trust . PS5 jailbreaks remain firmware-dependent and can carry risks beyond software instability. A compromised console may potentially expose account credentials, save data, and other stored information, particularly if users enable FTP access or install untrusted homebrew.

Playden clearly won't replace a gaming PC or a Steam Deck for most people . Its compatibility list is still incomplete, performance has not been verified for many games, and major DRM-protected releases remain off-limits.

Still, it is a notable development on the PlayStation 5 homebrew scene . A jailbroken PS5 can now browse and download a user's Steam library, run Windows games through Wine-based translation layers, and even integrate those titles into the console's native interface. Combined with the earlier Xbox Cloud Gaming client and ongoing emulation work, it reinforces the sense that PS5 homebrew is becoming increasingly capable.

About the author : With over two decades of experience in gaming journalism, Alessio Palumbo has led the gaming vertical at Wccftech since August 2015. He started working at a young age for Italian websites like Everyeye.it, Gamestar.it, Nextgame.it, and Multiplayer.it before kickstarting the indie English-language publication Worlds Factory as its founder and Editor in Chief. In the last decade, he has coordinated the overall output of Wccftech's gaming section, managed PR relations, assigned reviews, produced daily news coverage, edited gaming content as needed, and delivered game reviews. Arguably, his trademark content is the long series of exclusive developer interviews that have been cited by Wikipedia and by the biggest news media and gaming publications. His passion for technology also makes him knowledgeable when it comes to gaming hardware and tech. His favorite genres include RPGs, MMORPGs, and action/adventure games.

In the City of (Broken) Dreams, it’s not about how you flatline. What matters most is the impact you make with the time you’re given. 

So how will you seize the new opportunities awaiting for you in Night City? 

Check out the launch trailer celebrating both the second installment in the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime series, available now on Netflix, as well as Cyberpunk 2077 and its newly released update, featuring content inspired by the show.

Learn more about the new content and features the Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) introduces to the game in the official patch notes:

items.title: Check out what's coming to Cyberpunk 2077 in the Edgerunners 2 Update!
items.summary: Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you! Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watc
items.content:
Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you!

Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watch the Features Overview video to see some of the new features in action:

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

    [/*]

Quality of Life

  • Saves in the “Load Game” menu are now grouped by separate playthroughs.

    [/*]

  • Added item filters to apartment and vehicle stashes.

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where enabling Film Grain had no effect.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where controller settings for the Third-Person Camera were missing.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several typos in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added various other fixes for features and content introduced since Patch 2.1.

    [/*]

items.content:
To survive in Night City, you need someone to watch your back. On the way to the major leagues, V managed to gather a remarkable crew. You could even say, a crew to remember!

From trusted allies to unforgettable personalities, these are the people who helped shape V’s journey through the City of Dreams. This episode of It’s All About You is dedicated to the legendary crew that stood by V through every high and low.

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk 2077 in the most creative ways possible. Don’t forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY

See you in the next episode!

items.title: It’s All About You! — Never Fade Away
items.summary: Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥 Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey! Sure, th
items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.
